<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds an opt-in env var, `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MEGA_MOE_FUSE_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`. With it set, `--moe-backend aiter_mega_moe` (#59685) runs DeepSeek-V4's shared expert inside AITER MegaMoEV2, as one extra local expert per EP rank, instead of as a separate FP8 MLP after the MoE. This is the ROCm counterpart of the DeepGEMM MegaMoE shared-expert fusion (#53040), using the same extra-slot scheme as sglang on ROCm (sgl-project/sglang#35619).

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4-Pro on MI355X (DEP8): decode **ITL drops 4–9%** at concurrency 1–64 and **2–5%** at 128.
- **Output throughput rises 3–8%** at concurrency 1–64. At concurrency 128 the gain is small (+1–2%).
- Accuracy is unchanged:
  - Thinking mode: GPQA-Diamond 0.894 → 0.899 (official Think High 89.1) and MMLU-Pro 0.852 → 0.854, both within 1σ.
  - GSM8K stays within stderr, and NIAH is 1.00 from 4k to 128k context.
- With the env var unset, behavior is unchanged.

## Performance

**Setup**
- Hardware and model: MI355X ×8, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`.
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-7d0b4e57…`, the merge base of this PR, with the PR files mounted.
- Serving flags, aligned with the AgentX DEP8 recipe:
  - `--data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend mori_high_throughput --moe-backend aiter_mega_moe`
  - `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --async-scheduling --gpu-memory-utilization 0.86 --no-enable-prefix-caching`
- Benchmark: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --ignore-eos --num-prompts max(16, 4×conc)`.
- Baseline and fused ran on the same node with identical flags; only the env var differed.

| 128 | 3358 → 3380 (+0.7%) | 36.4 → **35.4 (−2.7%)** | 35.8 → **34.9 (−2.4%)** | 38.8 → **37.6 (−3.0%)** | 39.1 → 38.7 (−1.0%) | 1765 → 2194 |

Each point is a single run. In an earlier same-node session, two baseline runs differed by ≤0.6% in median ITL; with default flags that session also showed −4% to −7% ITL and +4% to +8% throughput at concurrency 1–128. TTFT is prefill/queue dominated and noisy at these prompt counts; the 1k/1k conc-128 TTFT increase did not reproduce at 8k/1k.

## Accuracy

All runs use the AgentX DEP8 server flags from the Performance section; baseline and fused differ only in the env var.

**Thinking mode, official sampling settings** (vLLM's default `reasoning_effort=high`, `temperature=1.0, top_p=1.0`, `--reasoning-parser deepseek_v4`, chat completions)

| Eval | Baseline | Fused | Official V4-Pro (Think High / Max) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| GPQA-Diamond (official `Idavidrein/gpqa`, 198 q, 0-shot, 128k output cap) | 0.8939 ± 0.0219 | **0.8990 ± 0.0215** | 89.1 / 90.1 |
| MMLU-Pro (12,032 q, 0-shot, 64k output cap) | 0.8524 ± 0.0032 | **0.8536 ± 0.0032** | 87.1 / 87.5 |

- **Prompt:** the simple-evals format, ending in `Answer: $LETTER`; the score is the `Answer:` line of the final content. Choices are shuffled with a fixed seed, so both arms see identical prompts.
- **Arms:** baseline and fused are within 1σ on both evals. GPQA-Diamond matches the official Think High score.
- **Truncation:** responses still thinking at the output cap are scored wrong:

  | | Baseline | Fused |
  |---|--:|--:|
  | GPQA-Diamond | 9/198 (4.5%) | 7/198 (3.5%) |
  | MMLU-Pro | 450/12,032 (3.7%) | 425/12,032 (3.5%) |

  Excluding them, MMLU-Pro is **0.886** (baseline) vs **0.885** (fused), so the ~1.7-point gap to the official number is the output cap, not the fusion. The official Think Max setting recommends a ≥384K context.

**Non-thinking / short-budget A/B** (same node and image for both arms)

| Eval | Baseline | Fused |
|---|--:|--:|
| GPQA-Diamond (InferenceX prompt, greedy, 16k output cap) | 0.6717 ± 0.0335 | 0.6768 ± 0.0333 |
| GSM8K (5-shot, flexible / strict) | 0.9575 / 0.9568 | 0.9477 / 0.9484 |
| NIAH 4k (RULER, 8 tasks × 100) | 1.00 (single_1: 0.99) | 1.00 |
| NIAH 16k (8 tasks × 100) | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| NIAH 64k (8 tasks × 50) | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| NIAH 128k (8 tasks × 25) | 1.00 | 1.00 |

- **GPQA at 16k is truncation-limited:** about half the responses hit the 16k cap mid-reasoning. On the ones that finished, accuracy is 96% in both arms. The row is only an A/B comparison; use the thinking-mode table above for absolute scores. Its data is the ungated `fingertap/GPQA-Diamond` mirror of the same 198 questions.
- **NIAH:** lm-eval's RULER needle tasks (`niah_single_{1,2,3}`, `niah_multikey_{1,2,3}`, `niah_multiquery`, `niah_multivalue`), one run per context length.
- **GSM8K:** `lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5`. The difference is about 1.2σ; #59685 reported 0.9484 for the unfused MegaMoE path.
- **MMMU / MMMU-Pro:** not applicable, because DeepSeek-V4-Pro is text-only (`DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`, no vision encoder).

## Details

- **Routing:** each rank holds 48 routed + 1 shared expert, so the kernel runs with `experts=392, topk=7`. A small Triton kernel remaps routed id `e → e + e // 48` and appends `ep_rank * 49 + 48` with weight 1.0. The routed weights already include `routed_scaling_factor`. The shared route always stays on the token's own rank, so it adds no all-to-all traffic.
- **Weights:** the shared MLP loads as usual. When MegaMoE weights are finalized, its block-FP8 weights are requantized to MXFP4 (`scaled_dequantize` + `mxfp4_quantize`, i.e. aiter `dynamic_mxfp4_quant`) into the shared slot, and the MLP is dropped. MTP and DSpark layers go through the same finalize path.
- **Tradeoffs:**
  - The shared expert runs at MXFP4 instead of FP8 (about 12% relative weight error), the same format the routed experts use.
  - `topk=7` needs a larger MoRI heap, so its default rises from 8G to 16G when the flag is on.
- **Known issue, not introduced by this PR (ROCm hipBLASLt):** with the default `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, startup can hang in the profile run on MI355X, with or without this flag, on the unmodified image too.
  - **Root cause:** hipBLASLt 1.2.2 (ROCm 7.2.3) keeps Stream-K fixup flags in one per-handle `Synchronizer` that every stream shares. DSv4's CSA layers run the two compressor `torch.mm` calls (N=2048 and N=512, fp32 out) concurrently on two aux streams with the same torch handle. At ≥12288 tokens per rank, the N=512 GEMM picks a Stream-K remainder kernel (`…SK3_SKFTR0_SKXCCM8`). One kernel can then clear a flag the other is waiting on, and that workgroup spins in `label_SK_Fixup` forever (seen with rocgdb). The other ranks then wait in the MegaMoE collective. It is not a MegaMoE bug.
  - **Fix:** ROCm/rocm-libraries#10951 (per-stream Stream-K flags) and #11691 (gfx950 cross-XCD flag coherence). Neither is in ROCm 7.2.3 or 7.2.4.
  - **Workaround until a ROCm release includes them:** `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192` (the AgentX recipe). At that size the N=512 GEMM never takes the remainder path, and every run started reliably.

**Tests:** `pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_aiter_mega_moe.py` passes on MI355X (6 passed). The new `test_shared_expert_route_appended` covers the id remap, `-1` padding routes, and the appended shared route. The end-to-end EP8 path needs 8× gfx950 and the DSv4 checkpoint, so it is validated outside CI (results above).

**Not a duplicate:** the existing MegaMoE shared-fusion PRs are NVIDIA DeepGEMM (#53040, #56568, #59927) or Kimi K3 (#53556). #53847 targets the non-mega AITER fused-MoE path.

Requantizing shared experts just to fuse the shared experts has been known to cause large accuracy degradation, that is why AITER later developed a heterogeous fused shared expert MoE kernel instead of requantizing the shared experts.

@tjtanaa Thanks. NIAH: I ran lm-eval's RULER needle tasks (`niah_single_{1,2,3}`, `niah_multikey_{1,2,3}`,` niah_multiquery`, `niah_multivalue`) at 4k, 16k, 64k and 128k context, one run per length. Samples per task: 100 at 4k and 16k, 50 at 64k, 25 at 128k.

In thinking mode, GPQA-Diamond (0.894 → 0.899) and MMLU-Pro (0.852 → 0.854) are also unchanged; see the reply above. I see no accuracy cost from requantizing the shared expert on these evals.

- FHMoE. Agreed, keeping the shared expert in FP8 is the better design. AITER's FHMoE (aiter/fhmoe.py, MXFP4 routed + FP8 shared) does this, but for the non-EP fused-MoE path. It isn't designed for MegaMoEV2.
- MegaMoEV2 can only fuse the shared expert by requantizing it today. This PR targets MegaMoEV2, the DP+EP fused dispatch/GEMM/combine path. MegaMoEV2 has no heterogeneous slot: every slot goes through one a8w4 kernel. So under aiter_mega_moe, requantizing to MXFP4 is currently the only way to fuse the shared expert. SGLang's MegaMoE shared-expert fusion on ROCm does the same (_maybe_load_fp8_shared_expert_as_fp4).
- The fusion stays opt-in. It is off by default (VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MEGA_MOE_FUSE_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 to enable), so users choose. Across the evals below, the accuracy impact is within noise:

| Eval	| Baseline |	Fused |
|---|---|---|
| GPQA-Diamond (thinking; official V4-Pro Think High: 89.1)|	 0.894 | 0.899 |
|MMLU-Pro (thinking, 12,032 q)| 	0.852	| 0.854 |
| GSM8K (5-shot) |	0.958 |	0.948 (~1.2σ) |
| NIAH (RULER, 4k–128k)	| 1.00	| 1.00|

In exchange, decode ITL drops 4–9% and throughput rises 3–8%.

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds an opt-in env var, `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MEGA_MOE_FUSE_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`. With it set, `--moe-backend aiter_mega_moe` (#59685) runs DeepSeek-V4's shared expert inside AITER MegaMoEV2, as one extra local expert per EP rank, instead of as a separate FP8 MLP after the MoE. This is the ROCm counterpart of the DeepGEMM MegaMoE shared-expert fusion (#53040), using the same extra-slot scheme as sglang on ROCm (sgl-project/sglang#35619).

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4-Pro on MI355X (DEP8): decode **ITL drops 4–9%** at concurrency 1–64 and **2–5%** at 128.
- **Output throughput rises 3–8%** at concurrency 1–64. At concurrency 128 the gain is small (+1–2%).
- Accuracy is unchanged:
  - Thinking mode: GPQA-Diamond 0.894 → 0.899 (official Think High 89.1) and MMLU-Pro 0.852 → 0.854, both within 1σ.
  - GSM8K stays within stderr, and NIAH is 1.00 from 4k to 128k context.
- With the env var unset, behavior is unchanged.

## Performance

**Setup**
- Hardware and model: MI355X ×8, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`.
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-7d0b4e57…`, the merge base of this PR, with the PR files mounted.
- Serving flags, aligned with the AgentX DEP8 recipe:
  - `--data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend mori_high_throughput --moe-backend aiter_mega_moe`
  - `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --async-scheduling --gpu-memory-utilization 0.86 --no-enable-prefix-caching`
- Benchmark: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --ignore-eos --num-prompts max(16, 4×conc)`.
- Baseline and fused ran on the same node with identical flags; only the env var differed.

**ISL 1024 / OSL 1024**

| Conc | Output tok/s | Median TPOT (ms) | Median ITL (ms) | P99 ITL (ms) | Median E2EL (s) | Median TTFT (ms) |

| 1 | 37.9 → **40.6 (+7.0%)** | 26.2 → **24.5 (−6.4%)** | 26.2 → **24.5 (−6.5%)** | 26.8 → **24.9 (−6.9%)** | 27.0 → **25.3 (−6.4%)** | 181 → 180 |
| 32 | 1002 → **1044 (+4.1%)** | 30.8 → **29.1 (−5.6%)** | 30.3 → **29.0 (−4.5%)** | 32.7 → **31.3 (−4.3%)** | 32.7 → **31.3 (−4.2%)** | 1166 → 998 |
| 64 | 1911 → **1974 (+3.3%)** | 32.2 → **30.9 (−4.1%)** | 32.1 → **30.7 (−4.3%)** | 34.6 → **33.3 (−3.8%)** | 34.3 → **33.0 (−3.7%)** | 1117 → 1146 |
| 128 | 3358 → 3380 (+0.7%) | 36.4 → **35.4 (−2.7%)** | 35.8 → **34.9 (−2.4%)** | 38.8 → **37.6 (−3.0%)** | 39.1 → 38.7 (−1.0%) | 1765 → 2194 |

**ISL 8192 / OSL 1024**

| Conc | Output tok/s | Median TPOT (ms) | Median ITL (ms) | P99 ITL (ms) | Median E2EL (s) | Median TTFT (ms) |
|:-:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 16 | 445 → **471 (+5.7%)** | 32.2 → **29.7 (−7.8%)** | 29.1 → **27.3 (−6.1%)** | 32.4 → **30.4 (−6.1%)** | 36.7 → **34.9 (−5.0%)** | 4080 → 3792 |

| 128 | 2478 → 2518 (+1.6%) | 47.4 → 46.7 (−1.5%) | 34.6 → **32.7 (−5.4%)** | 1020 → 1015 | 52.7 → 52.2 (−1.1%) | 4138 → 4175 |

Each point is a single run. In an earlier same-node session, two baseline runs differed by ≤0.6% in median ITL; with default flags that session also showed −4% to −7% ITL and +4% to +8% throughput at concurrency 1–128. TTFT is prefill/queue dominated and noisy at these prompt counts; the 1k/1k conc-128 TTFT increase did not reproduce at 8k/1k.

## Accuracy

All runs use the AgentX DEP8 server flags from the Performance section; baseline and fused differ only in the env var.

**Thinking mode, official sampling settings** (vLLM's default `reasoning_effort=high`, `temperature=1.0, top_p=1.0`, `--reasoning-parser deepseek_v4`, chat completions)

| Eval | Baseline | Fused | Official V4-Pro (Think High / Max) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| GPQA-Diamond (official `Idavidrein/gpqa`, 198 q, 0-shot, 128k output cap) | 0.8939 ± 0.0219 | **0.8990 ± 0.0215** | 89.1 / 90.1 |
| MMLU-Pro (12,032 q, 0-shot, 64k output cap) | 0.8524 ± 0.0032 | **0.8536 ± 0.0032** | 87.1 / 87.5 |

- **Prompt:** the simple-evals format, ending in `Answer: $LETTER`; the score is the `Answer:` line of the final content. Choices are shuffled with a fixed seed, so both arms see identical prompts.
- **Arms:** baseline and fused are within 1σ on both evals. GPQA-Diamond matches the official Think High score.
- **Truncation:** responses still thinking at the output cap are scored wrong:

  | | Baseline | Fused |
  |---|--:|--:|
  | GPQA-Diamond | 9/198 (4.5%) | 7/198 (3.5%) |
  | MMLU-Pro | 450/12,032 (3.7%) | 425/12,032 (3.5%) |

  Excluding them, MMLU-Pro is **0.886** (baseline) vs **0.885** (fused), so the ~1.7-point gap to the official number is the output cap, not the fusion. The official Think Max setting recommends a ≥384K context.

**Non-thinking / short-budget A/B** (same node and image for both arms)

| Eval | Baseline | Fused |
|---|--:|--:|
| GPQA-Diamond (InferenceX prompt, greedy, 16k output cap) | 0.6717 ± 0.0335 | 0.6768 ± 0.0333 |
| GSM8K (5-shot, flexible / strict) | 0.9575 / 0.9568 | 0.9477 / 0.9484 |
| NIAH 4k (RULER, 8 tasks × 100) | 1.00 (single_1: 0.99) | 1.00 |
| NIAH 16k (8 tasks × 100) | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| NIAH 64k (8 tasks × 50) | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| NIAH 128k (8 tasks × 25) | 1.00 | 1.00 |

- **GPQA at 16k is truncation-limited:** about half the responses hit the 16k cap mid-reasoning. On the ones that finished, accuracy is 96% in both arms. The row is only an A/B comparison; use the thinking-mode table above for absolute scores. Its data is the ungated `fingertap/GPQA-Diamond` mirror of the same 198 questions.
- **NIAH:** lm-eval's RULER needle tasks (`niah_single_{1,2,3}`, `niah_multikey_{1,2,3}`, `niah_multiquery`, `niah_multivalue`), one run per context length.
- **GSM8K:** `lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5`. The difference is about 1.2σ; #59685 reported 0.9484 for the unfused MegaMoE path.
- **MMMU / MMMU-Pro:** not applicable, because DeepSeek-V4-Pro is text-only (`DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`, no vision encoder).

## Details

- **Routing:** each rank holds 48 routed + 1 shared expert, so the kernel runs with `experts=392, topk=7`. A small Triton kernel remaps routed id `e → e + e // 48` and appends `ep_rank * 49 + 48` with weight 1.0. The routed weights already include `routed_scaling_factor`. The shared route always stays on the token's own rank, so it adds no all-to-all traffic.
- **Weights:** the shared MLP loads as usual. When MegaMoE weights are finalized, its block-FP8 weights are requantized to MXFP4 (`scaled_dequantize` + `mxfp4_quantize`, i.e. aiter `dynamic_mxfp4_quant`) into the shared slot, and the MLP is dropped. MTP and DSpark layers go through the same finalize path.
- **Tradeoffs:**
  - The shared expert runs at MXFP4 instead of FP8 (about 12% relative weight error), the same format the routed experts use.
  - `topk=7` needs a larger MoRI heap, so its default rises from 8G to 16G when the flag is on.
- **Known issue, not introduced by this PR (ROCm hipBLASLt):** with the default `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, startup can hang in the profile run on MI355X, with or without this flag, on the unmodified image too.
  - **Root cause:** hipBLASLt 1.2.2 (ROCm 7.2.3) keeps Stream-K fixup flags in one per-handle `Synchronizer` that every stream shares. DSv4's CSA layers run the two compressor `torch.mm` calls (N=2048 and N=512, fp32 out) concurrently on two aux streams with the same torch handle. At ≥12288 tokens per rank, the N=512 GEMM picks a Stream-K remainder kernel (`…SK3_SKFTR0_SKXCCM8`). One kernel can then clear a flag the other is waiting on, and that workgroup spins in `label_SK_Fixup` forever (seen with rocgdb). The other ranks then wait in the MegaMoE collective. It is not a MegaMoE bug.
  - **Fix:** ROCm/rocm-libraries#10951 (per-stream Stream-K flags) and #11691 (gfx950 cross-XCD flag coherence). Neither is in ROCm 7.2.3 or 7.2.4.
  - **Workaround until a ROCm release includes them:** `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192` (the AgentX recipe). At that size the N=512 GEMM never takes the remainder path, and every run started reliably.

**Tests:** `pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_aiter_mega_moe.py` passes on MI355X (6 passed). The new `test_shared_expert_route_appended` covers the id remap, `-1` padding routes, and the appended shared route. The end-to-end EP8 path needs 8× gfx950 and the DSv4 checkpoint, so it is validated outside CI (results above).

**Not a duplicate:** the existing MegaMoE shared-fusion PRs are NVIDIA DeepGEMM (#53040, #56568, #59927) or Kimi K3 (#53556). #53847 targets the non-mega AITER fused-MoE path.

> @AMD-yanfeiwang Thanks for the work. But adding this will quant the shared expert from `mxfp8 -> mxfp4`. Need more tests on other benchmarks? May run more comparition on `GPQA-D` and `MMMU-PRO` evals?

@benenzhu Thanks for the review. I added GPQA-Diamond and MMLU-Pro in thinking mode, with the official sampling settings, plus NIAH.

- Baseline and fused ran on the same node and image with the same flags (AgentX DEP8 + --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4). The only difference is `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MEGA_MOE_FUSE_SHARED_EXPERTS`.

- Settings: thinking mode at vLLM's default `reasoning_effort=high, temperature=1.0, top_p=1.0`, 0-shot simple-evals prompt.

- GPQA-Diamond matches the official Think High number.

- MMLU-Pro is ~1.7 points below official in both arms. 3.5–3.7% of responses were still thinking at the 64k cap, and those are scored wrong. Excluding them, baseline/fused are 0.886/0.885. The official Think Max setting recommends a ≥384K context.

- MMMU-Pro doesn't apply here: DeepSeek-V4-Pro is text-only (DeepseekV4ForCausalLM, no vision encoder).

Full setup and per-eval details are in the PR description's Accuracy section.

> > But adding this will quant the shared expert from `mxfp8 -> mxfp4`. Need more tests on other benchmarks?
> > May run more comparition on `GPQA-D` and `MMMU-PRO` evals?
> 
> @AMD-yanfeiwang please disclose NIAH accuracy and more comparisons. Requantizing shared experts just to fuse the shared experts has been known to cause large accuracy degradation, that is why AITER later developed a heterogeous fused shared expert MoE kernel instead of requantizing the shared experts.

@tjtanaa Thanks. NIAH: I ran lm-eval's RULER needle tasks (`niah_single_{1,2,3}`, `niah_multikey_{1,2,3}`,` niah_multiquery`, `niah_multivalue`) at 4k, 16k, 64k and 128k context, one run per length. Samples per task: 100 at 4k and 16k, 50 at 64k, 25 at 128k.

In thinking mode, GPQA-Diamond (0.894 → 0.899) and MMLU-Pro (0.852 → 0.854) are also unchanged; see the reply above. I see no accuracy cost from requantizing the shared expert on these evals.

- FHMoE. Agreed, keeping the shared expert in FP8 is the better design. AITER's FHMoE (aiter/fhmoe.py, MXFP4 routed + FP8 shared) does this, but for the non-EP fused-MoE path. It isn't designed for MegaMoEV2.
- MegaMoEV2 can only fuse the shared expert by requantizing it today. This PR targets MegaMoEV2, the DP+EP fused dispatch/GEMM/combine path. MegaMoEV2 has no heterogeneous slot: every slot goes through one a8w4 kernel. So under aiter_mega_moe, requantizing to MXFP4 is currently the only way to fuse the shared expert. SGLang's MegaMoE shared-expert fusion on ROCm does the same (_maybe_load_fp8_shared_expert_as_fp4).
- The fusion stays opt-in. It is off by default (VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MEGA_MOE_FUSE_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 to enable), so users choose. Across the evals below, the accuracy impact is within noise:

| Eval	| Baseline |	Fused |
|---|---|---|
| GPQA-Diamond (thinking; official V4-Pro Think High: 89.1)|	 0.894 | 0.899 |
|MMLU-Pro (thinking, 12,032 q)| 	0.852	| 0.854 |
| GSM8K (5-shot) |	0.958 |	0.948 (~1.2σ) |
| NIAH (RULER, 4k–128k)	| 1.00	| 1.00|

In exchange, decode ITL drops 4–9% and throughput rises 3–8%.

Full setup and per-eval details are in the PR description's Accuracy section.
